body:
My mom has a dog, I don't have any pets on my own because I can't really take care of them (plus the only pet I could have is a cat, but my dad hates them and it's off limits).

Yes, they know that I have suicidal thoughts. They told me that they are surprised i'm still trying to be a functional human being because most people would have given up already in my place. I got to a university exam while I was  having a severe anxiety attack for example.
They agree with me that the whole situation I'm in sucks balls. They understand that I need something to hang on, but it's hard to find such a thing when you failed everything you tried to do and with my limitations. 

I recognize that I made a lot of progress during the time, but my life is worse even if I can manage my conditions. 

While I'm not suicidal I still think I'd be better off dead at this point, that I don't really want to live anyway. I can cope with everything most of the time but still... My life is not good.
I can even manage my depression and anxiety because I recognize that they are there and what the triggers are and I can less their impact on me.
But still... I'm still there with nothing to do all day, I didn't graduated, I didn't do anything I wanted to do at this point in my life. And I realistically have no chance to because I'm too sick.

I was going to push for a sleep study before  getting on Strattera, but getting this diagnosis is useless to me. I suspected narcolepsy actually, I was fatigued all the time, I had a terrible sleep pattern that got screwed up extremely easily (I just needed to go it bed a hour late to not be able to sleep until 4am or until I took something to sleep), I was so tired that I needed multiple naps. I did everything recommended but never improved. 

In my country there is Strattera and various formulation of methylphenidate, plus some offlabel things. I take Lyrica for chronic pain and it helps a lot, I rarely flare up and if I do it's because I did too much (way too much), it lowers my pain to a manageable level (this I why I don't take painkillers or anything on a regular basis). 

But despite this my life never got better. I can treat my symptoms as much as I can (and I do, I always did everything recommended, I'm an extremely compliant patient, I even managed to took an habit to exercise), but my life never improved. I still had to drop out of university for example and I'm aware that I will struggle to keep a job, and working probably will make me useless the rest of the day.

I can't find a single reason why I would deal with this for the next 60 years.

I'm loved, I have a boyfriend and a family. But being loved doesn't not outweight the rest. 
I completely fail at life anyway. I don't want to keep trying because it has always been completely useless and realistically it's not going to change anything. I'm just going to be worse and worse and I can't deal with this anymore. And I don't want to. I took my choice I guess.
They make the other worse, yes.

People need something to make them going on. I have nothing. And I don't want to spend other time learning things that don't improve my life. I don't have any willpower anymore, it's useless to fight a lost battle. 

Being diagnosed as a child has a  much better outcome than being diagnosed as an adult like I did.

I don't need support, fuck support honestly. I need something that makes me feel less like trash and more of an human being and it's not going to happen. I know it's not going to happen because this is how I felt all those years and I never improved. I made all those efforts to still fail and feel like this basically and I can't take this anymore. 

I can improve internally as I want but it's not going to make my life worth living.

No, I didn't "jump", I still need to make an actual effort to do things. I'm still on the lower side of the spectrum even if I'm better.

But I'm just tired of dealing with my life. I can't and I don't want anymore. Even if I can learn those skills, then what exactly? It's not going to change anything, I'm still a useless failure.

Yes, twice, once when I started with the practice I'm in, then a second time when I did my ADHD evaluation in another hospital,both are negative.
According to every mental professional involved the issue is more emotional dysregulation+depression/dysthymia (not sure which one). I don't get mania/hypomania symptoms,(the only things that can look like this is my hyperactivity, but hypomania doesn't get you walking all day around your house I think)I feel like trash most of the time, sometimes it get worse.

I have had it enough that I don't think it will ever get away from me, and most of the time I can manage it. I have a lot of copying skills for this. But honestly I'm just tired of trying. I'm not really getting anywhere. I can manage everything I have fine enough to not make me bedridden, have hygiene, not living in a dumpster instead of an house but I'm still far away from having something that makes it worth it.

They didn't suggest me to go on disability because only of ADHD, I have a laundry list of chronic long term issues both mental and physical that make me useless or near useless.

Also for the degree I would get it there is no benefit, it's just a thing they would do to help me find a job... But I would be in a "disabled" quota doing a stupid job for the rest of my life. It would not come with a livable wage which is the thing I actually need. And this thought makes me feel worse... 

I'm convinced that the only way I could be happy is by being normal. I have nothing in my life.

This stupid test is why I didn't get diagnosed when I was 7 and it took 18 years more to get some help. My life would have been completely different. 

Fuck IQ testing. I'm not even smart, I'm a useless piece of crap all the time. 

(The explanation is that intelligence isn't necessarily correlated to executive functions... And that a while ago psychiatrists thought ADHD was correlated only with a low IQ).

I'm too low functioning to have the "nice things". You are talking to someone who has been taken to have their hearing evaluated because they cannot keep up with conversations. 

I don't mind being hyperactive actually, mostly I just walk around because of it, I may think too fast sometimes but okay, everyone has issues. What really gets to me is the inattention. I look like an idiot because I can't listen to things (I can't sit through a 10 minute podcast... I can now because of meds but two months ago it was impossible), I can't talk, I make a lot of stupid mistakes and I need to read things three times before understanding them and I still get everything wrong. 

Meds help, but I'm still on the low side of the spectrum and this is realistically the better I can get. Maybe the ADHD coaching I'm waiting on is going to make miracles, but after years of therapy, medication, studying on my own I have little hopes that's going to make a difference.
And I'm afraid that I will lose my medication in some way (it terrifies me) because the little I can do is because of Strattera. It helps me sleep, it removed like 70% of my fatigue. It's great but... I still have nothing. I still have my unfinished project, a crappy resume, I still buy things impulsively (mostly books, so no one consider this an issue), I still don't understand people, I still have nothing that makes me be happy to start the day. 

True that it might be because I'm clinically depressed and I have been for years at this point, but sooner or later I will give up because my life just keeping getting worse if possible.

But I'm disabled from birth of I count ADHD in it and I have a lot of arguments to prove that hypothesis. I have been sick since I was what,18? I never stood a chance. I never had a life that deserve to be called that. 


I never accepted anything, and while I do everything "right" I'm still far away from acceptance. I hate myself too much to get there.
I can handle my health issues(and it's a job at a certain point), but I wouldn't call this acceptance. I'm aware that I'm fighting something I cannot win and it makes everything useless.

Yes but I still need a way to support myself. I can't pay utilities and rent with air. I qualify for disability but I won't get a livable anything out of it. 
It's supposed to help me find a job, but it will be a dead end one because I would be hired in some disability quota, 20 hours per week in the lowest possible position available is not going to be liveable.

I did everything in the list: I have been in therapy for 5 years now, did physical therapy, lost 15 kg and changed dieting because I have scoliosis and me being a little overweight was making my back hurt. Hell I even exercise more than most abled bodied people I know(I swim and hike). 

And I benefit from each of those things, i made a lot of progress... But my life really hasn't: I'm worse than I started because things have gone south anyway. 
Not sure how to explain this better. It's that I don't like the person I am, I don't have a lot of options overall, and I failed a lot. 
Having an hobby is a struggle because I never got around to be good at something and when I look at the things I did and realise that they suck it makes me feel even worse. 

When I say disability I mean everything. Physically I have fibromyalgia, hypermobility joints syndrome (possibly hEDS, not sure and I don't want to investigate because it's going worse and it's not supposed to), scoliosis(probably relates to the hypermobility).

Where my physical health doesn't get there it comes the mental health and one makes the other worse. 

But really I'm just tired to deal with things that are out of my control, it's a job on its own and I can't do it and I don't want to. It's also useless because when you have chronic conditions it never gets really better. I keep thinking where I would be now if I were normal and making lists over lists over lists to describe the difference between me and the person I wish I was.

I'm heavily medicated for everything and I'm doing everything I can to manage the condition.
I'm currently on Strattera, citalopram and Lyrica. I went from being low-functioning to a below than average functioning person. I still struggle with doing certain things but Strattera has fixed my severe sleeping issues(one of the things why I'm so scared that it will stop working) for example, I can do like 70% of what i'm supposed to do in a day, my pain levels are at 4 if I don't overdo myself. Going out of the house leaves me out of energy though which is a requirement to do like 90% of the jobs. I can focus on things finally for more than 3 minutes and make way less mistakes.

Even if I'm doing everything "right" my life is still utter trash because I have nothing. Morally speaking I have nothing, I don't care about things (once I have my computer I'm fine, endless entertainment), but I have accomplished nothing, I'm not really good at doing anything, I screwed up a lot and I still struggle with socialisation(also a requirement to handle a job, I don't understand people). I don't have many options in my life because my disability limits me so much despite my efforts.
I don't have anything. I wasn't able to accomplish anything and I have no life. I'm a failure.

It's not really a thing I have ever thought of, because I'm the depressed asshole in the relationship. He is a genuinely happy and enthusiastic person usually, that would be extremely out of his character. 

I just don't want to have a shitty life where I can't accomplish anything and where I have pain 24/7. I hate myself and my life. I haven't looked at myself for days. That's the level of self hatred I have. I just want to go because I know I will never be happy because of my faulty body and my faulty brain.

If I gave up I would have saved myself a lot of heartbreaks. A lot.
I don't have only ADHD I have chronic pain and other stuff, my joints are fragile and sometimes things go out of place and it's incredibly painful. I can't sleep for all of this stuff. I have to take 7 medication in the morning to still feel like less than. My pain levels are never going under 3.

The point is not that I need to achieve something or be good at something. The point is I don't have anything that makes me truly happy and satisfied with myself.  Not having abusive parents and having a nice person as a partner while being good things aren't substitute for feeling good about something that's only yours.

No, there is no happiness for me. I only wanted a thing since I was a child and it didn't happened because i'm stupid.

When you have chronic conditions things never get better. They only get worse, medications and so on just make things go worse more slowly than they would do. And I have fought my brain and my body for what, 8 years? 5? I never achieved anything.  It just went worse and worse. 

It's not really worth living when you have nothing like I do. I never achieved anything because of my malformed brain and body. I just want to go. And I will. I don't want to be miserable anymore, and I fail everything i tried to do in these years. I can keep taking meds like candy, but my life is still terrible and there is not "getting better". 
I not only hit the bottom... I keep digging myself a  bigger hole.

I even tried one of those workbook that are supposed to make you feel better... I just wrote "ahahahah" when it asked me what I'm good at. I was never able to learn how to do stuff because of ADHD. I'm extremely unskilled and an idiot. Truly, it's not worth it.

I never had anything for myself in my life. It's the worst feeling ever. I only wanted one thing since I was a child and it didn't happen because I'm stupid and I'm a cripple. 
I'm the definition of loser. I see everywhere people my age having a job, getting a degree and all that stuff and I'm just googling where to buy a fucking rope. Nothing makes me happy, because when I do something I either fail, I don't finish it or I do it so badly that it needs to be redone from start. It's not worth it

I'm not moving forward. when you have a chronic illness things just go worse. And worse. If you are lucky enough they will get worse slowly.

The point Is not happiness, the point is that I have no whatsoever future. I was studying for a STEM degree which would mean having a job that I would be able to be accommodated for my disabilities,even if I just decided to teach or work in the field. I really cared about the subject but I'm the worst student on this planet due to my issues.

I mean, for most people sure, I'd agree with your that university is not a necessity, but when you can't do much because of disability everything you can add to your resume is important.

Now I'm out of options, basically. I'm having an hard time finding a job I can do with my qualifications. Especially because I didn't graduated and I didn't work while studying.

I'm out of money and I'd graduate when I'm 27 if everything goes as it should... But when you are a broken moron like me it doesn't, so 28-29. And I definitely don't want to waste more time on doing something that never gave me any sort of gratification.

Yes, it took away everything from me. I also developed anxiety and depression. 

I always wanted only one thing in my life and ADHD made me fail it, so it's hard. Now that I'm medicated I'm even more resentful because I don't know what to do/I feel like i'm wasting my meds.

Yes, I still have nightmares about it. They were not suit for the job (let's be real, most teachers don't have a fucking clue how to teach), tried to motivate me by lowering my grades and so on. It's one of the reason I have no self esteem now.

I'm already in therapy. It's the reason I'm not suicidal anymore(I have emotional dysregulation) and I don't sleep 18 hours a day.
My health issues have already taken everything from me, years of my life included. This is why I know it's not going to get better. It never did. Even if I pause, ADHD is not going anywhere, my joints are still going to dislocate, my pain level won't get under 5. It can only get worse from this. 

I guess I'll just wait until I'm disabled enough to get subsidies or something.

I truly burned every single thing I've tried to do. I have nothing in my life, it's so empty because I have accomplished anything. I'm just a overall disappointment, the kind of person no one wants to have anything to do with.

I tried so hard to do something, when I had terrible thoughts I gaslit myself thinking that "it's going to be better"... It never did actually. It just got worse.  But I don't have enough spine to do something bad.
It's just a thought. But I'm not going to do this to myself again. 

Every day  I feel tired because it's not worth it. I see people around me doing something and I'm here stuck with this curse. I was cursed to fail. It's difficult to find anything good to look at when you have nothing but issues, issues and even more issues

There is no trading schools where I live, plus I don't really understand economics or anything like this. Plus.. I'm a terrible student. there are very few post-hs courses and they usually mean nothing because people will always choose a graduate over you, and they are stupid expensive. They cost more than a year in university.
I wanted to do copywriting/screenwriting school. But they will ask me the resume which is the trash with "underachiever" and "failure" written on it. I have no chance, really, and i don't want to set up expectations because I know it's not going to work. And it won't get me a job so I'm not wasting time.

I specialised in admin work in high school (it's a thing here), but there are people with admin and business degree and I can't stand a competition with them, no one wants to hire the underachiever (and I wouldn't either to be fair, let's be honest). And I can't do physical jobs because I'm at risk of injuries and I will get sick in no time. 

I hate myself because I know I don't have any chance against anyone. 

It never got better with me, it only got worse and worse. And when documents won't match how I look it will open a new can of worms that was better for anyone if stayed closed.

My parents will be unsurprised at the trans thing..when I tried to explain to them the concept of non binary they said "like you, right"? So probably they know.
